name: Murder at the Manor
description: A guest lies dead at the manor. Each suspect was in a different room with a different motive. Work out whodunit.
clues: Either Ravenscroft goes with Gardening or Conservatory goes with Grimsby.
Ashford goes with at least one of Study, Veranda, or Gardening.
Library, Study, and Gardening go with Grimsby, Pierce, and Ravenscroft, in some order.
Between Pierce and Ravenscroft, one goes with Gardening and the other with Writing.
Exactly two of these are true: Ashford goes with Bathing; Grimsby goes with Library; Conservatory goes with Cooking.

hints.text: Suppose Ashford went with Study — following the clues from there hits a contradiction, so it doesn't.
chain: Start by assuming Ashford goes with Study.
Study goes with Ashford, so Grimsby can't go with Study.
Study goes with Ashford, so Pierce can't go with Study.
Study goes with Ashford, so Ravenscroft can't go with Study.
…but now the clue “Library, Study, and Gardening go with Grimsby, Pierce, and Ravenscroft, in some order” can no longer hold — a contradiction.
So Ashford does not go with Study.
